ledger.note: 1243: Rao Siha establishes the Rathore state at Pali. 'established in Pali by Rao Siha' (the text dates the founding to 1243; the infobox says '1226-1273'); Siha died fighting a Muslim force in 1273.
1395: Chunda shifts the capital to Mandore. 'He shifted his capital to that city in 1395'; Zaffar Khan besieged Mandore in 1396 and was repelled.

1395: Mandore joins the state as a dowry. 'Chunda married in a Parihar Rajput clan from which he received the city of Mandore as Dowry'; 'He shifted his capital to that city in 1395'; Dhuhar had captured Mandore in 1291 and it was later lost (Marwar page, read again 2026-10-20). The page dates the capital move, not the marriage, so 1395 is the page's year for the move. [Repair 2026-10-20: counterpart was 'nobody'.]

region.text: Mandore and the site of Jodhpur (the Mandore circle, short of Pali)

ledger.note: 1438: Mandore passes to Mewar. 'Rana Kumbha, son of Mokal, got him [Ranmal] assassinated in 1438' (Marwar page); Jodha 'escaped Mewar' and regained Mandore only 'by 1453'; the Rana Kumbha page: 'In 1453 AD, he was able to capture his ancestral capital of Mandore from Mewar'. The Marwar page does not say that Mewar occupied it; 1438 is Ranmal's death, a bridging year, and Mewar is the Rana Kumbha page's holder. Mirrors the gain in kingdom-of-mewar.

region.text: Mandore and the site of Jodhpur

ledger.note: 1453: Jodha regains Mandore from Mewar. 'In 1453 AD, he was able to capture his ancestral capital of Mandore from Mewar' (Rana Kumbha page); the Marwar page: 'by 1453, he was able to regain Mandore'. In 1459 'Rao Jodha' changes the capital to Jodhpur, which 'took its name from its founder'. [Repair 2026-10-20: counterpart was 'nobody'; the loss of 1438 was missing.]
1459: Jodha founds Jodhpur and moves the capital there. 'to Jodhpur in 1459 by Rao Jodha'.

ledger.counterpart: Nagaur (Daulat Khan) and Ajmer (Biram Dev of Merta)
ledger.note: 1534: Maldeo takes Nagaur and Ajmer. 'In 1534 Maldeo attacked Nagaur and forced Daulat Khan to flee to Ajmer'; Ajmer was 'captured from Biram Dev of Merta' (Marwar page: 'Maldeo captures Ajmer and Nagaur' 1534-35).

1538: Maldeo conquers Jalore. 'Maldeo successfully conquered Jalore and took Sikandar as a prisoner to Jodhpur.' [Reviewer sa-04-x, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 to 2: the Maldeo page dates only the attack ('In 1538 he defeated Mahecha Rathores and annexed Siwana and sent Bida Rathore to attack Jalore'); the conquest of Jalore is undated]

region.text: Tonk and Toda (Bayana is not drawn)

ledger.counterpart: Afghan nobles of Tonk and Toda (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1539: Maldeo takes Tonk and Toda. 'In 1539 Maldeo took advantage of the war between the Mughals and the Sur Empire to conquer Bayana, Tonk and Toda'; the holders are not named.
1542: Maldeo annexes Bikaner. 'Rao Maldeo took advantage of this situation to annex the entire kingdom of Bikaner' after the Battle of Sohaba against Rao Jaitsi.

region.text: Marwar from Ajmer to Mount Abu; Ajmer and Nagaur are recorded as lost to Haji Khan (below), not occupied

ledger.note: 1544: Sher Shah's generals take Marwar. 'Khawas Khan Marwat and Isa Khan Niyazi took possession of Jodhpur and occupied the territory of Marwar from Ajmer to Mount Abu in 1544' after the Battle of Sammel (the Marwar page: Sher Shah occupies Jodhpur for 'several months'). [Repair 2026-10-20: Ajmer and Nagaur moved to the loss event beside this one.]

1544: Haji Khan Sur takes Ajmer and Nagaur. 'Haji Khan was a slave of Sher Shah Suri and became the lord of Ajmer and Nagaur after the Battle of Sammel' (1544); 'Maldeo reoccupied his lost territories in 1545' names neither, and 'The Mughals conquered Ajmer and Nagaur in 1557' (from Haji Khan). Replaces the loss to the Mughals dated 1557.

region.text: Marwar; Ajmer and Nagaur stay with Haji Khan

ledger.note: 1545: Maldeo retakes his lands. He 'regained his lost territories in 1545 after Sher Shah Suri's death' (the Marwar page: Maldeo retakes Jodhpur in 1545). [Repair 2026-10-20: Ajmer and Nagaur removed: they did not return.]

ledger.counterpart: Bhati and local holders (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1550: Maldeo takes Pokhran and Phalodi.
1557: Maldeo takes Merta at Harmoda. 'Together their armies defeated Udai Singh in January 1557 in the Battle of Harmoda'; 'Maldeo captured the fortified city of Merta after the battle'.

region.text: Jodhpur and the lands of Marwar

ledger.note: 1564: the Mughals take Jodhpur and Marwar. 'Mughal forces occupy Jodhpur after Chandrasen rejects Akbar's suzerainty' (1563-64); Maldeo died on 7 November 1562 and a 'fratricidal contest began for the throne'. The remnant at Bhadrajun is drawn until 1570.
1571: Chandrasen is dislodged from Bhadrajun. 'Chandrasen was dislodged from Bhadrajun by a Mughal contingent' (1570-71).

region.text: Marwar, restored as a Mughal state

ledger.note: 1583: Akbar recognises Udai Singh. 'Akbar recognises Udai Singh as ruler as a Mughal state' (1583); the state is a Mughal vassal, a tint in the Mughal dossier.

1583: Udai Singh rules Marwar as Akbar's vassal. 'In 1583, Akbar formally recognized Chandrasen's rival brother Udai Singh as the ruler of Marwar as a Mughal state'; Udai Singh was 'restored to the throne as a vassal' after the annexation of 1581. Recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord); the mughal-empire owner should carry the mirror entry. [Repair 2026-10-20: new event; the gain of 1583 had no vassal event.]
1650: Jaswant Singh takes Pokhran from the Bhatis. 'Jaswant Singh takes Pokhran from the Bhatis' (1650).
1679: Aurangzeb takes Marwar. 'Aurangzeb converts Marwar into crown territory after Jaswant Singh's death' (1678-79); Ajit Singh was born in 1679.
1679: Marwar becomes Mughal crown land, ending the vassalage of 1583. 'Aurangzeb converts Marwar into crown territory after Jaswant Singh's death' (1678-79).
1681: Durgadas begins to recapture Marwar. 'Durgadas recaptures much of Marwar' (1681-1687); Marwar and Mewar were defeated at Debari in 1680.
1707: Ajit Singh takes Jodhpur. 'After Aurangzeb's death, Ajit Singh captures Jodhpur' (1707-08).
1707: Jodhpur is Ajit Singh's. 'After Aurangzeb's death, Ajit Singh captures Jodhpur' (1707-08).
1708: Bahadur Shah takes control of Marwar. 'Bahadur Shah takes control of Marwar in February 1708.'

1710: Bahadur Shah recognises Ajit Singh. 'Bahadur Shah recognises Ajit Singh as ruler of Jodhpur' (1710). The Marwar page also has a settlement 'ratified by Ajit Singh on 19 March 1714' under which he was to 'pay a peshkash or tribute to the emperor' and give a daughter to Farrukhsiyar (married 11 December 1715): a second Mughal tributary period that is not modelled because no page dates its end.

6 January 1818: Man Singh accepts the British alliance. 'The British had no role in the state's affairs until 6 January 1818, when the Raja at that time, Man Singh, entered into a subsidiary alliance'; 'The British will protect the principality and territory of Jodhpur'; 'Man Singh will act in subordinate cooperation'. Recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord); 'british-empire' is the Cliopatria row of 1757-1858, and the owner of the East India Company or the Raj should carry the mirror entry. [Repair 2026-10-20: new event.]

1947: British suzerainty ends as Jodhpur accedes. The infobox has 'Acceded to the Dominion of India: 1947-1949' and the instrument was signed on 11 August 1947; the end of the state is 1949 (dissolve).

1949: Jodhpur accedes to India. The infobox ends 'Acceded to the Dominion of India' with '1947-1949'; Hanwant Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 11 August 1947. The end year follows the same convention as Mewar.

wars.outcome: The Mughals took Ajmer and Nagaur (1557), occupied Jaitaran (1558) and Jodhpur (1563-64), and dislodged Chandrasen from Bhadrajun (1570-71); Udai Singh was recognised as a Mughal ruler in 1583.

wars.outcome: Aurangzeb took Marwar in 1678-79; Durgadas recaptured much of it in 1681-1687; Ajit Singh took Jodhpur in 1707-08; Bahadur Shah recognised him in 1710.

wars.name: Maratha-Jodhpur wars
wars.outcome: Scindia's Marathas fought Jodhpur with defeats at Patan and Mertia in 1790; the page gives no border change.

notes:
No Cliopatria row (Cliopatria lacks Marwar). Two pages: Marwar Kingdom (long, with the dated chronicle) and Maldeo Rathore; the 'Mughal-Rathore War' page does not exist under that title. The Marwar page's infobox area is 93,424 km2 (no year); the final shape (the gazetteer's Marwar region with Nagaur, Jalore, Barmer, Pokhran and Phalodi) comes to about that (see the keyframe). Earlier keyframes are circles round the places the pages name.
The sa-05-x batch (Rajput states from 1526) may also carry this state: check polities/ before editing.
Disagreements: founding 1243 (text) against '1226-1273' (infobox); Maldeo's accession 1531 (Marwar page) or 9 May 1532 (his page); the accession to India 1947 (instrument signed 11 August 1947) or 1949 (infobox); the Maldeo page puts the Tonk, Toda and Bayana conquests in 1539, the Marwar page lists none of them; the Marwar page dates the Bikaner annexation to no year (Maldeo page: 1542).
Not settled: the Bikaner split (undated on the Marwar page; Bika, Jodha's son); Mandore before 1395 (Dhuhar took it in 1291 and lost it); Chunda's hold on Nagaur (he died defending it in 1428); Mughal occupation of Jaitaran (1558); Chandrasen's holdings after 1570-71 (empty keyframe 1571-1582); the extent of the restored Marwar of 1583 and 1710 (the gazetteer region is a reading); Ajit Singh's reign dates (1708-1724 per the text, with 1707 as capture); Abhay Singh, Ram Singh (1749-1751, missing from the page's list); the Maratha war of 1787-1791 (Patan and Mertia 1790, no land); the subsidiary alliance of 6 January 1818 (the vassal event belongs to british-empire); the ruler strip uses death years for the early reigns (Asthana, Jalansi, Chhada).
Counterparts needing a dossier: bikaner (Rathore state, 1488-1949; annexed by Maldeo 1542), jaisalmer (Bhatis), sur-empire (sa-05-b), mughal-empire (sa-05-a), maratha-empire (sa-05), british-empire for 1818 (sa-06), republic-of-india.
Gazetteer names needed: Pali, Nagaur, Jalore, Merta, Pokhran, Phalodi, Bhadrajun, Barmer.

[Repair 2026-10-20, sa-04-x-fix] Applied: (1) Ajmer and Nagaur: the Maldeo Rathore page has Haji Khan, Sher Shah's slave, 'lord of Ajmer and Nagaur after the Battle of Sammel' (1544); the 1557 loss to the Mughals is replaced by a 1544 loss to sur-empire (confidence 3), and the two are out of the occupation of 1544-1545, out of the keyframes from 1544 and out of the 1557 text (the Mughals took them from Haji Khan). (2) Mandore: a 1438 loss to kingdom-of-mewar (confidence 2, Ranmal killed 'in 1438') and the 1453 regain now has kingdom-of-mewar as its counterpart on the Rana Kumbha page ('capture his ancestral capital of Mandore from Mewar'); the keyframe of 1395-1452 is split at 1438 and the Mandore capital has a gap 1438-1452. The Marwar page itself does not say that Mewar held Mandore, and its infobox calls Marwar a 'vassal state of the Kingdom of Mewar (1428-1458; 1508-1527)', which is not modelled. (3) Mandore 1395 came as a dowry from the Parihars (counterpart 'Parihars of Mandore'). (4) Vassal events from the vassal's side: Mughal 1583 to 1679 and British 6 January 1818 to 1947; the second Mughal period (settlement of 19 March 1714 with peshkash) is not modelled because no page dates its end. (5) Thin items: the Rao Sheoji (Siha) page gives Pali in 1243 and no extent, so the Pali circle is still a reading; the Bikaner State page dates the founding of Bikaner to 1465 by Rao Bika, a son of Jodha, 'whereupon he founded his own kingdom' (the Marwar page puts Bika's siege of Jodhpur under Suja, 1492-1515); Bikaner's land was never drawn as Marwar's before 1542, so there is no split event. Bikaner needs a dossier (founded 1465). (6) The Sirohi (Mewar) and Jalore (Marwar) circles overlap at the frontier in 1538-1563 (about 5,000 km2), see kingdom-of-mewar.
